sentences: A restricted-isometry matrix approximately preserves the Euclidean lengths of all sparse vectors.
The source seeks deterministic or certifiably correct constructions with nearly linear dependence on sparsity in their row count.
It also asks whether suitably chosen rows of Fourier or other bounded-entry unitary matrices can achieve the desired bounds.
A related computational obstacle is multiplying a selected Fourier submatrix by a vector faster than the straightforward quadratic method.
These questions connect explicit measurement design with the recovery time needed by deterministic heavy-hitter and sparse-reconstruction algorithms.
